final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral USMCA package with 75% auto RVC, wage-floor labor inspections, integrated wage+RVC audits by a single third-party auditor, a 16-year term with review gates at years 6 and 11, and a binding labor-environment panel. Canada secured Chapter 19 for auto disputes only; dairy was deferred to separate bilateral talks within 90 days. All three governments committed to initial the text by end of day after 90-minute review.
minority_objections: Dairy_ag initially demanded Canada open supply-managed dairy market as part of the trilateral text, but was overruled by Congress and USTR who deferred dairy to separate bilateral talks
key_conflicts: Canada's Chapter 19 red line vs. USTR's demand to eliminate binational dispute panels entirely
Dairy market access vs. Canada's domestic political constraints on supply management
Dual vs. integrated inspection regimes for wage and RVC compliance
key_concessions: USTR accepted Chapter 19 for auto disputes only (not full commercial claims)
Canada accepted 75% RVC and wage floor in exchange for Chapter 19 carve-out and dairy deferral
All parties accepted integrated single-auditor inspections to reduce compliance costs
USTR replaced hard 6-year sunset with 16-year term + review gates at years 6 and 11
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement for autos, dairy supply management off the table in trilateral text
USTR: No Chapter 19 for general commercial disputes, labor enforcement must have independent audit authority
Congress: Automatic wage inspections with real fines and production halts, or no ratification
Labor_union: Independent auditors with binding enforcement, not advisory panels
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Implementation timeline and transition costs for manufacturers to reorganize supply chains under new RVC rules
Political risk that dairy bilateral talks fail within 90 days and reopen the entire package
Ambiguity in 'certified third-party auditor' definition could create post-signature disputes over auditor qualifications
downstream_risk_variables: Dairy bilateral negotiation outcome within 90 days
Congressional ratification vote margin (depends on labor union support holding)
Manufacturer capital investment decisions hinge on clarity of integrated audit implementation
Canada's domestic ratification of Chapter 19 carve-out (auto-only vs. full commercial)
uncertainty_notes: The text must be drafted and reviewed by 6 PM same day; any deviation from locked language on auditor, calendar, or cost-split could collapse the deal. Dairy bilateral talks are a deferred landmine. The 16-year term with review gates reduces sunset uncertainty but leaves open whether reviews become renegotiation triggers.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC and wage floor drove the entire negotiation structure; integrated wage+RVC audits became the mechanism that unlocked Canada's acceptance and resolved dual-compliance cost concerns
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Congress made independent wage inspections with production halts and real fines a ratification red line; labor_union demanded binding enforcement not advisory panels; this drove the integrated auditor compromise
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy was raised by dairy_ag as a blocking issue and initially by USTR as a price for Canada joining, but Congress and Canada deferred it to separate bilateral talks—acknowledged as sensitive but not allowed to block the trilateral
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 was non-negotiable and would not move on autos without it; USTR's refusal to allow full Chapter 19 nearly collapsed talks until the auto-only carve-out was accepted
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply_chain_mfr stated hard sunset freezes capital plans; USTR proposed 16-year term with review gates at years 6 and 11 (stay-in default) which was accepted by all parties as the solution to sunset uncertainty
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress explicitly conditioned ratification on independent audits, real fines, and exact language matching; labor_union stated labor won't support the deal without binding enforcement; this shaped every enforcement provision
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto_industry and supply_chain_mfr raised compliance costs, dual audit regimes, and capital freezes as concerns; these were acknowledged and addressed via integrated inspections, but implementation timeline and transition costs were not deeply negotiated
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico_neg explicitly stated 'Canada can join on the same terms Mexico took, or we sign without you'; USTR used the U.S.-Mexico bilateral as leverage to force Canada to accept 75% RVC and wage floor

node: Node 1 - North American Trade Negotiation Room (after the 27 Aug 2018 U.S.-Mexico preliminary agreement, before the final trilateral USMCA package; information cutoff 2018-08-27)
